introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.
incertitudes: Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, sans total par question. Le champ points de l'exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Given that $(x+2)$ is a factor of $f(x)$, where $f(x)=x^3+kx^2-10x-8$, find the value of the constant $k$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
By the factor theorem, $(x+2)$ is a factor of $f(x)$ if and only if $f(-2)=0$.

$f(-2)=(-2)^3+k(-2)^2-10(-2)-8=-8+4k+20-8=4k+4.$

$4k+4=0\Rightarrow k=-1.$

**$k=-1$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) With this value of $k$, factorise $f(x)$ completely. *[2 marks]*
(ii)(a) The quadratic equation $x^2+4x+1=0$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. State the values of $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$: sum of roots $=-\dfrac{b}{a}$, product of roots $=\dfrac{c}{a}$.

Here $a=1$, $b=4$, $c=1$.

**$\alpha+\beta=-4$ and $\alpha\beta=1$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) For the same equation $x^2+4x+1=0$ with roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$, write down another quadratic equation with roots $2\alpha$ and $2\beta$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
New sum of roots: $2\alpha+2\beta=2(\alpha+\beta)=2(-4)=-8.$

New product of roots: $(2\alpha)(2\beta)=4\alpha\beta=4(1)=4.$

A quadratic with sum $S$ and product $P$ of roots is $x^2-Sx+P=0$:

$x^2-(-8)x+4=0.$

**$x^2+8x+4=0$.**

Check: the roots of $x^2+4x+1=0$ are $-2\pm\sqrt3$; doubling gives $-4\pm2\sqrt3$, which are the roots of $x^2+8x+4=0$ (sum $-8$, product $16-12=4$).
